title: Core scalar Cech external cup compatibility
statement: Under the coefficient, comparison, and open-cover hypotheses of lem-sc-picard-scalar-cech-external-cup [lem-sc-picard-scalar-cech-comparison, lem-sc-picard-external-cech-cup-component], including iSup U = top and iSup V = top, the displayed natural-degree cycle compatibility formula holds. In particular, arbitrary open families that fail to cover are excluded: their comparison witnesses need not determine cohomology extensions away from their union.

proof.text: Destructure the degree summand as (p,q) with p+q=n, and substitute n. Set A and B to the factor scalar Cech complexes and h to the (p,q)-tensor summand inclusion followed by c.f (p+q). The prescribed component coordinates hc are exactly IsPicardExternalCechCupBidegree for h.

Define t = HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap c (p+q) z. Evaluate cyclesMap_i on z and use its supplied inclusion equation to obtain iCycles(t)=h(iCycles(a) tensor iCycles(v)). Evaluate homologyπ_naturality on z to obtain H(c)([z])=[t]. These are the existing Mathlib naturality identities.

Extract cX,cY,cP, their IsModuleCechComparison predicates and their scalar witness equations from heX(p), heY(q), heP(p+q). Choose the uniquely characterized ordinary module cup on the two projection pullbacks by exists_unique_moduleCupProduct. Apply picardModuleCech_externalPairing using both cover equalities, h with its prescribed coordinates, and the inclusion equation for t.

Evaluate the three scalar witness equations on the cycle classes. Apply congrArg to each module pullback and the proved private moduleCup_congr to the two inputs of cup. The product witness identifies eP([t]) with the resulting ordinary cup. scalarExternalCup_moduleComparison identifies that cup with externalCup of eX([a]) and eY([v]). Compose these equalities with H(c)([z])=[t]. Substitution of n has made the degree cast reflexive.

lean.statement:
theorem picardScalarCech_externalCup_core
    {k : Type w} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{w}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    {ι κ : Type w} (U : ι → X.Opens) (V : κ → Y.Opens)
    (hUc : iSup U = ⊤) (hVc : iSup V = ⊤)
    (c : HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor ((picardCechFunctor f U).obj F)
        ((picardCechFunctor g V).obj G) (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k))
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ) ⟶
      (picardCechFunctor (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
        (fun ij : ι × κ ↦ pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U ij.1 ⊓
          pullback.snd f g ⁻¹ᵁ V ij.2)).obj (externalCupCoefficients f g F G))
    (hc : IsPicardExternalCechCupComponent f g U V F G c)
    (eX : ∀ p : ℕ, ((picardCechFunctor f U).obj F).homology p →ₗ[k]
      scalarCohomology f F p)
    (heX : ∀ p, IsPicardScalarCechComparison f U F p (eX p))
    (eY : ∀ q : ℕ, ((picardCechFunctor g V).obj G).homology q →ₗ[k]
      scalarCohomology g G q)
    (heY : ∀ q, IsPicardScalarCechComparison g V G q (eY q))
    (eP : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((picardCechFunctor (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
        (fun ij : ι × κ ↦ pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U ij.1 ⊓
          pullback.snd f g ⁻¹ᵁ V ij.2)).obj
            (externalCupCoefficients f g F G)).homology n →ₗ[k]
        scalarCohomology (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) n)
    (heP : ∀ n, IsPicardScalarCechComparison (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
      (fun ij : ι × κ ↦ pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U ij.1 ⊓
        pullback.snd f g ⁻¹ᵁ V ij.2) (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) n (eP n)) :
    let A := (picardCechFunctor f U).obj F
    let B := (picardCechFunctor g V).obj G
    let T := HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor A B (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k))
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : {pq : ℕ × ℕ // pq.1 + pq.2 = n})
    (a : A.cycles i.val.1) (v : B.cycles i.val.2) (z : T.cycles n),
    T.iCycles n z = HomologicalComplex.ιMapBifunctor A B
        (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k)) (ComplexShape.up ℕ) i.val.1 i.val.2 n
        i.property ((A.iCycles i.val.1 a) ⊗ₜ[k] (B.iCycles i.val.2 v)) →
      eP n (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap c n (T.homologyπ n z)) =
        cast (congrArg (fun d ↦ ↥(scalarCohomology (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
          (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) d)) i.property)
          (externalCup f g F G i.val.1 i.val.2
            (eX i.val.1 (A.homologyπ _ a)) (eY i.val.2 (B.homologyπ _ v)))

statement_change.old_statement: Under the coefficient and comparison hypotheses of lem-sc-picard-scalar-cech-external-cup, without the cover equalities, the displayed cycle compatibility formula holds.
statement_change.what: Stage-3 repair in the legacy statement_change schema: restore both cover equalities omitted by the false below-unit helper. On P1_k with rational points x0,x1 and U=V=P1 minus x1, take F=G=k(x0) direct-sum k(x1). The global rings are k. Factor comparisons can extend s to (s,0), and a product comparison can extend s to (s,s,s,s), since their defining equations see only restriction to U or U times U. For the classes of 1 the external cup of the factor extensions is (1,0,0,0), whereas the product extension is (1,1,1,1). This is a mathematical counterexample, not a fully Lean-formalized scheme construction. The former disjoint Spec(k times k) example fails because ring-linear maps must respect global idempotents. The public enclosing theorem already assumes both cover equalities and keeps exactly its old signature.

old_proof.text: Fix the displayed degree, summand, cycles and total cycle. Expand the refinement and Alexander–Whitney coordinates and use the comparison witnesses; scalar restriction identifies the resulting cup with externalCup.
